name: Wunai Bunu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Yang, Zaibiao 2016. M nai yu yanjiu [A Study of the Mnai language]. MA thesis, Hunan Normal University, 266pp (Chinese; CNKI-only, not openly online)

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 613 (hdl:1885/146760, CC-BY).
sources.note: Comparative work; grep for Wunai / Hm Nai / Ng Nai / Longhui / 唔奈 gives zero hits, so Wunai is not among its data points. Only stress remarks are general (iambic weak-strong prefix+root pattern in Hmong-Mien, p. ~text line 1427; loanword stress in Thai). Nothing on Wunai stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page wuna1248 and reference record 669233.
sources.note: Classification (Bahengic, after Mao & Li 1997), alternative names (Hm Nai, Ngnai, Punu, Wu-nai, 布努語唔奈方言); only two descriptive refs, one of them (Lin & Luoerwu 2003 on Japhug) plainly misattributed. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Hm Nai language'; Wikipedia (zh) 唔奈语, 布努语, 巴哼语; Wikipedia (en) 'Pa-Hng language', 'Bahengic languages'; Wikidata Q56452.
sources.note: No phonology given for Wunai; reference lists only: Mao Zongwu & Li Yunbing 1997 巴哼语研究 (Shanghai Far East), Meng Chaoji 2001 瑶族布努语方言研究 (Minzu), Yang Zaibiao 2016. zh 巴哼语 page gives an 8-tone table for Pa-Hng (35 33 31 44 53...) but says nothing about stress and nothing phonological about 唔奈.

sources.citation: Yang, Zaibiao 杨再彪. 2016. 呣奈语研究 [A study of the Mnai (Wunai) language]. MA thesis, Hunan Normal University, 266 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only full-length modern description of the language (Glottolog's sole grammar-sketch entry); a 266-page Chinese thesis will have a 语音 chapter with tones and very likely a note on 轻声/重音 in disyllables. Named by the earlier scan too.

sources.citation: Sun Hongkai 孙宏开, Hu Zengyi 胡增益 & Huang Xing 黄行 (eds.). 2007. 中国的语言 [The languages of China]. Beijing: 商务印书馆 — chapter 唔奈语.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Handbook with a separate short chapter per language including 唔奈语 (initials, finals, tones, syllable structure); the most likely place for a one-line statement on stress/weak syllables if the thesis is unobtainable.

sources.citation: Chen Qiguang 陈其光. 2013. 苗瑶语文 [Miao-Yao languages]. Beijing: 中央民族大学出版社.

sources.citation: Mao Zongwu 毛宗武 & Li Yunbing 李云兵. 1997. 巴哼语研究 [A study of Pa-Hng]. Shanghai: 上海远东出版社. ISBN 7-80613-371-2.

sources.note: The work that established Wunai as Pa-Hng's closest relative; contains comparative Wunai material and is the classification source cited by Glottolog and Wikipedia.

sources.citation: Mao Zongwu 毛宗武, Meng Chaoji 蒙朝吉 & Zheng Zongze 郑宗泽. 1982. 瑶族语言简志. Beijing: 民族出版社 (rev. ed. 2009 in 中国少数民族语言简志丛书).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The classic 简志 treats 唔奈 (Longhui) as a Bunu dialect with its own phoneme/tone inventory; this is the primary source most later surveys copy.

sources.citation: Yang, Zaibiao. 2016. 呣奈语研究 [Ḿ nài yǔ yánjiū / A study of the Mnai language]. MA thesis, Hunan Normal University, 266 pp. (Chinese). Glottolog ref 669233, hhtype grammar_sketch.

sources.note: Only the Glottolog record was seen (no URL, no abstract). CNKI/Wanfang could not be reached from our machine (Wanfang search page renders empty; Bing/Baidu/DDG fronts bot-walled). Presumed to contain a 语音 chapter; whether it discusses 重音 is unknown.
